subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — request for emergency overflow authorization
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@corebank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, CoreBank Ops <ops@corebank.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Production latency and 500s on reserved pool — urgent

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We started seeing elevated tail latency and an increasing rate of 500s on our production inference endpoints around 08:45 UTC. Throughput on our reserved pool is falling ~30% below the committed rate, which is impacting live credit decisioning. Error traces point to timeouts in the dedicated GPU pool and queueing on your side.

Top-line impact: several downstream customers reported delayed approvals; our SLAs are at risk if this persists beyond the morning window. Ops has a running dashboard and I can share access; I included ops@ for visibility.

What we need immediately:
- Quick confirmation that you see the same metrics on your side
- Short-term mitigation (route to fallback, temporary capacity bump, anything that avoids customer-facing failures)
- A timeline for a durable fix and whether this will require changes on our side

Please advise — this is impacting live traffic.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
VP Product Operations, CoreBank
elena@corebank.com

Attachment: grafana-snapshot.png (overview of the spike)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@corebank.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, CoreBank Ops <ops@corebank.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:24:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency and 500s on reserved pool — urgent

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging and apologies for the impact. We’re seeing the same tail latency and elevated 5xx rate on CoreBank’s reserved capacity. I’ve looped in David (serving/runtime) and Marissa (CS lead) and Aditya (capacity/infra) to triage.

Immediate plan (first 30–45min):
- Investigate root cause (David) and surface queue/backpressure metrics
- If confirmed, enable emergency overflow to Redwood-hosted replicas for a short window (requires your approval) to stop customer-facing errors
- Throttle non-critical batch traffic originating from CoreBank’s scheduled jobs (we can coordinate limits)
- Prepare a capacity bump on the reserved pool as a parallel mitigation (Aditya)

Can you confirm: are you ok with an emergency overflow to our hosted pool for up to 30 minutes? That will route inference to hosted model replicas — we will not persist any additional customer data beyond normal telemetry and will keep access logs for the standard retention period. We’ll also prepare an incident link and share metrics.

Standby for a technical update from David in the next ~10 minutes.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:33:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency and 500s on reserved pool — urgent

Folks — quick notes after initial inspection (09:30 UTC):
- Observed symptom: a sustained spike in request concurrency from CoreBank’s prod key starting 08:42 UTC. Queue depth in the dedicated GPU pool rose to 14x normal for the 16GB replica group. KPIs: avg service latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~820ms; 5xx rate rose to 4.3% (baseline ~0.1%).
- Root signals: simultaneous increase in batch sizes from a scheduled scoring job plus a KV cache eviction loop. The combination is causing memory pressure and frequent kernel context switches on the pool’s GPUs.
- Evidence: attached corebank-metrics-0900-logs.tar.gz (profile + kernel traces) and snapshot link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/incident/corebank-20280302 (read-only).

Short-term mitigations I recommend now (can be done within 10–20 min):
1) Enable emergency overflow (route a configurable portion of CoreBank traffic to hosted replicas) — low risk, quick.
2) Reduce batch-size ceiling for CoreBank’s reserved endpoints to 1.5x baseline to limit queue depth (we can do this unilaterally but will notify CoreBank).
3) Temporarily relax quantization fallback that surfaced in v1.2 deployment (roll back to previous profile) — this reduces memory churn but will increase per-token cost slightly.
4) Aditya: if you can add +2 GPU capacity to the reserved pool as hot spare, that will buy headroom for the 90–120 min window.

I’ll continue to collect traces and will post an initial incident doc.

— David Kim
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachments: corebank-metrics-0900-logs.tar.gz, grafana-snapshot.png

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@corebank.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, CoreBank Ops <ops@corebank.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: Production latency and 500s on reserved pool — urgent

Forwarding technical readout and proposed mitigations. TL;DR: we can stop customer-facing errors quickly by enabling emergency overflow for up to 30 minutes and applying two short-term config changes (batch cap + rollback of the quantization profile). Aditya is standing by to add hot-spare capacity if needed.

Request for your approval:
- Authorize Redwood to enable emergency overflow to hosted replicas for up to 30 minutes (routes inference only — no long-term data transfer)
- Authorize Redwood to throttle/adjust batch ceilings on your reserved endpoints for the next 2 hours to stabilize queues

We’ve attached the emergency fallback playbook for transparency. If you approve, we’ll execute immediately and share a separate incident link with live metrics.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

1) Does the overflow path move any PII or payloads outside of our VPC boundaries? We must ensure no traffic leaves our network in cleartext or is stored in a way that violates our data policy.
2) My leadership is asking whether this incident will trigger any SLA credits — please start the review process and let me know the timeline for a postmortem.

Appreciate the quick response — please confirm and execute.

— Elena

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 13:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency and 500s on reserved pool — urgent

Elena — thanks for the quick decision and sorry again for the disruption. Confirmations and next steps: 
- Overflow behavior: traffic routed to Redwood-hosted replicas will remain encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. No raw customer payloads are exported outside of the agreed deployment topology. For this overflow we will not create any new long-term external backups; short-lived telemetry and traces used for debugging are retained under the existing retention policy. I’ve asked Security to produce a short statement for your records and copied in David to include any technical guarantees.
- Execution: we have enabled overflow at 10:12 UTC and applied the batch ceiling change at 10:14 UTC. Early metrics show 5xx rate dropping toward baseline and median latency improving. Aditya added +1 GPU hot spare at 10:20 UTC.
- SLA credits & postmortem: I opened a formal postmortem request and HubSpot ticket HS-134582. Marissa will coordinate the credits review and timeline; we’ll aim to share a preliminary incident summary within 24 hours and a full postmortem within 72 hours.

I’ll keep this thread updated as we have more telemetry. If you want a short sync with your ops/infra leads, we can set one up within the next hour.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
